{{Short description|Austrian and British mathematician (1930–2000)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Ascher Otto Wagner''' (12 October 1930, in [[Vienna]] – 27 May 2000, in London) was an Austrian and British [[mathematician]], specializing in the theory of [[finite group]]s and [[finite projective plane]]s. He is known for the {{ill|Dembowski–Wagner theorem|de|Satz von Dembowski-Wagner}}.<ref>{{cite journal
   |author=Dembowski, P.
   |authorlink=Peter Dembowski
   |author2=Wagner, A.
   |title=Some characterizations of finite projective spaces
   |journal=Archiv der Mathematik
   |volume=11
   |year=1960
   |pages=465–469
   |doi=10.1007/BF01236976
   |mr=0143095 |s2cid=122535748
 }}</ref>

Ascher Wagner received his Ph.D. in 1958 with the dissertation ''Some Problems on Projective Planes and Related Topics in the Theory of Algebraic Operations'' supervised by [[Kurt Hirsch]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=79949|title=Ascher Otto Wagner}}</ref> Wagner was a faculty member at the [[University of London]] and then at the [[University of Birmingham]].

In 1958 he married Gillian Mary Jaidka (1929–1993) in [[Hampstead, London]].
